implementation_notes: TypeScript gives the best static signal of any language here: `noUnusedLocals` and `noUnusedParameters` are compiler options, and `tsc --noEmit` plus a bundler's tree-shake report give the rest. For exported-but-unused symbols the compiler will not complain (an export is a public surface by construction), so a dedicated tool — `knip`, `ts-prune`, or the `import/no-unused-modules` ESLint rule — is the instrument. The two TypeScript-specific anchors are barrel files that re-export everything (so the graph looks used) and ambient declarations in `.d.ts` files that nothing references but which still shape the whole codebase's types.
idiom_name: unused export, unused npm dependency, unused type-only file
pitfalls: Barrel `index.ts` re-exports make every symbol appear imported somewhere, which defeats `noUnusedLocals`.
A `.d.ts` ambient declaration shapes the type system for the whole program with no import statement.
Types used only via `extends`/implements on a conditional type can be referenced with no syntactic mention.
